issue_context.title: Make PubTernal classes properly internal
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Localization/Localization/src/ResourceManagerStringLocalizer.cs#L57

This will involve a breaking change announcment.

There are few more related to localization:

member | details 
-- | --
api/Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerStringLocalizer.-ctor.yml | 2 invalid cross   reference(s)   "Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.Internal.AssemblyWrapper",   "Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.Internal.IResourceStringProvider".
api/Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerStringLocalizer.GetStringSafely.yml | 1   invalid cross reference(s)   "Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerStringLocalizer._resourceManager".
api/Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerStringLocalizer.yml | 1   invalid cross reference(s)   "Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerStringLocalizer._resourceManager".
api/Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerWithCultureStringLocalizer.yml | 1   invalid cross reference(s)   "Microsoft.Extensions.Localization.ResourceManagerStringLocalizer._resourceManager".

review_comments: What's the replacement for this? Should we move this to a public namespace?

To my thinking it doesn't need replacing. It's an internal interface whose only purpose was to give us a point to create fakes for our integration tests. If anyone was using this interface to use something other than a `ResourceManager` as the backing for their [ResourceManagerStringLocalizer](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Localization/Localization/src/ResourceManagerStringLocalizer.cs) I would advise them that they should instead create an entirely new implementation of `IStringLocalizer`, since `ResourceManagerStringLocalizer` makes lots of assumptions based on the behavior of `ResourceManager`.
